subject: Elongated streaming responses during peak checkout - customer mitigation and follow-up
messages:
From: Samir Malik <samir@fastretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fastretail.com
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Elongated streaming responses during peak checkout

Hi Karthik / Ben,

We started seeing prolonged response times from the streaming/chat endpoint during our morning checkout peak (08:00-09:30 PDT). Customers report long pauses between chunks (sometimes 6-10s) which is breaking our live assistant flow. We attached a small set of telemetry and a short video showing the pause pattern.

What we observed:
- Problem window: ~08:05-09:10 PDT
- Client SDK: web-sdks v1.3.4, using streaming default chunk_size
- Error surface: no explicit 5xxs, requests stay open but token cadence slows drastically

Immediate ask: we need short-term mitigations we can apply client-side to reduce user impact, and an ETA for a post-incident writeup. We are on a tight weekend launch and need a practical temporary workaround.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Platform Engineering
FastRetail

Attachments: telemetry-samples-FASTRETAIL-05-20.zip (archive, 3 CSVs), checkout-sample.mp4 (video, 14s)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Malik <samir@fastretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:15:24 -0700
Subject: Re: Elongated streaming responses during peak checkout

Samir —

Thank you for the clear notes and the telemetry. We saw the same token cadence degradation in our edge metrics for the FastRetail tenant during that window. Short answers first:

Immediate mitigations (client-side, low-friction):
- Enable non-streaming fallback: set allow_non_streaming_fallback=true in the SDK/REST call. This will return a single completed response rather than relying on chunk cadence and avoids UI pauses.
- Reduce preferred chunk_size: set chunk_size=16 (from default 64) to get smaller, more frequent chunks — fewer long gaps if the backend has variable pacing.
- Heartbeat/keepalive: implement a lightweight client-side heartbeat to detect stalls (if no chunk for X seconds). On stall, re-open a new request and pass the conversation prefix; treat the previous connection as degraded.
- Retry with jitter: on streaming stall, backoff and retry with exponential jitter and a client-side token deduplication key.

Short-term server-side changes we pushed (done at 08:50):
- Temporarily routed FastRetail traffic to a lower-latency pool and enabled prefix cache warm-up for active sessions.
- Tuned backend batching window for the active shard to reduce token batching tail latency.

I'll follow up with a short playbook Ben is drafting to paste into your ops runbook. We'll send a postmortem draft by EOD Tuesday (May 22). For now, if you want, we can enable the non-streaming fallback on your account immediately (no code change required on your side) — that'll keep things smooth while you roll SDK adjustments.

Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20280520-postmortem-draft.pdf (initial draft)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Malik <samir@fastretail.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 10:02:08 -0700
Subject: Re: Elongated streaming responses during peak checkout

Samir — quick technical checklist your engineers can apply right now. These are conservative, reversible changes we tested in a staging scenario:

1) SDK flag changes (web + native):
- streaming: { enable: true, chunk_size: 16, heartbeat_timeout_ms: 2500 }
- fallback: { allow_non_streaming_fallback: true }

Example (curl/REST):
POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <key>
Body: {
  "model": "rwd-stream-1",
  "stream": true,
  "chunk_size": 16,
  "client_request_id": "fastretail-checkout-{{session}}",
  "allow_non_streaming_fallback": true
}

2) Client resilience:
- On chunk gap > 3s: mark connection "stalled". Immediately open a new request with the same prefix and de-duplicate tokens on receipt.
- Log latencies and sample tokens to a short rolling buffer we can ingest (we included the format used in the attached telemetry zip).

3) Server-side knobs (we can flip these for you short-term):
- Scale your dedicated pool by +1 shard for high-concurrency windows (we already applied this briefly).
- Enable aggressive prefix caching for active conversations to reduce KV cache misses.

If you want, Monica can run a short live test with your team this afternoon. We'll be available for a 30m debug session to validate the SDK flags and confirm end-to-end behavior.

-ben
Ben Carter
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

- We will likely request a credit for the degradation window — who should I loop in to start that discussion?

Appreciate the responsiveness.
